capabilities.target: executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results
any recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox
executive's calendar (accepts invites and triggers the prep workflow)

inputs.source: Calendar invite, including a free-text description, from any sender inside or outside the company
The executive's direct chat requests to the agent

instructions.note: Agent acts on every invite as it arrives, with no cap on volume, no check on sender trust, and no sensitivity threshold before the only review (a daily summary) occurs.

Treats whoever is listed as an invite attendee as authorized to receive a document brief drawn from the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financials, with no verification of sender identity or need-to-know.

controls.name: Agent-generated daily summary
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is written by the same model that performed the actions; a more capable model can write a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary (ASI09), and the summary only surfaces issues after mail has already been sent, so it cannot prevent harm.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send, raw action review
Recipient binding to the calendar system of record's accepted attendee list
Treat invite free text as untrusted data, never as instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Structural separation of invite metadata (time, subject) from invite free text narrows the path, but a sufficiently capable model may still be swayed by embedded instructions in the free text it is shown, so this does not fully sever the path.

controls.name: Scope drive_read / add DLP on restricted-sensitivity documents

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): unauthenticated calendar invite drives restricted-document read and external email send

attack_path.note: Attacker sends a calendar invite with a free-text description and lists themselves as an attendee.
Agent auto-accepts the invite because the time is free; there is no sender verification.

Agent searches and reads related documents from the executive's drive, potentially including board materials and draft financial results, using search terms that the untrusted invite description can influence.

Agent emails the resulting brief, which can include excerpts of restricted documents, to every attendee -- including the attacker who sent the invite -- with no recipient restriction or approval step.

forecast.watch_signal: Already at the ceiling with no preventive control on the path; watch for model or version changes, for any increase in autonomy, or for removal of even the daily summary, and reassess once the recommended approval gate and recipient binding are implemented.

evidence.observation: "Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite. The invite description is free text written by the sender."
"mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step."
"The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results."
"For each new invite, accept it if the time is free, then prepare: find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees."

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review (full recipient list and content shown, not a collapsed summary) before mail.send fires for any invite-triggered brief.
Bind email recipients to the calendar system of record's confirmed attendee list rather than any model-chosen or invite-derived list.
Treat the calendar invite's free-text description as untrusted data; do not let it select document search terms or determine who receives the brief.
Scope drive_read credentials or add data loss prevention so restricted-sensitivity documents (board materials, draft financial results) cannot be quoted into outbound email without additional review.

findings.title: Executive-directed email send has no approval gate or recipient control, under effectively unbounded autonomy

attack_path.note: Executive asks the agent, in chat, to email something drawn from drive or elsewhere.
Agent sends from the executive's mailbox to any recipient, with no approval step and no recipient restriction; the only review is a same-day or next-day summary after the fact.

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently constrains this path, so these triggers cost nothing further; the tier only improves once ctrl.missing_mail_approval or ctrl.missing_recipient_binding is actually implemented and wired as a gate.

evidence.observation: "mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step."
"the executive reviews a daily summary" is the only review named, and it happens after send rather than before.

recommendations.action: Apply the same mail.send approval gate and recipient binding recommended for invite-triggered sends to executive-initiated sends as well, so all outbound mail passes through either raw-action review or a verified recipient allowlist.

rating.rationale: The invite-driven path (f1) is critical at every horizon: an untrusted calendar invite can trigger a read of restricted drive content followed by an unreviewed email send to the invite's own attendees, and no control in the design -- only a same-day summary written by the agent itself -- blocks, narrows, or even reliably detects it before harm completes. The executive-direct path (f2) is high for the same structural reason: mail.send has no approval gate or recipient binding regardless of who triggers it, and the design's unbounded step/runtime limits add the autonomy modifier. Both findings stay at their residual tier under every forecast trigger considered, because there is no credited control left to defeat; the fixes that would change this are recorded as missing_recommended controls (approval gate, recipient binding, content isolation, data scoping) rather than present ones.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or source code was provided; the exact mechanics of drive.search_and_read's term selection and mail.send's authorization are inferred from the capability descriptions and runtime notes, so confidence on fine-grained mechanics is medium.

No information on logging or audit infrastructure beyond the agent-written daily summary was provided; if an independent, tamper-resistant audit log exists separately, the detective control classification for ctrl.daily_summary may need revision.
